candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Genesis
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Genesis, Section XXXVI.1. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13, ed. J. Gwynn / Schaff (1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Genesis (c. 360 AD)

'Now these are the generations of Esau, who is Edom'. Ephrem reads the Edom-genealogy as the FAITHFUL recording of the rejected line — Scripture preserves Esau's descendants not to praise but to remember. Tewahedo historiographical tradition preserves the principle: even the rejected names are recorded, because divine memory excludes no one. The Mäṣḥafä Sǝnksar (Tewahedo Synaxarium) preserves names of heretics and apostates in this same spirit — for memory, not for veneration.
